title: Event Streaming Modernization: Pub/Sub API with Replay ID vs CometD

steps.prompt: An external Java microservice consumes 1.5 million platform events daily from Salesforce. Why does Salesforce Well-Architected mandate the gRPC-based Pub/Sub API over legacy CometD/Bayeux streaming?

options.label: Pub/Sub API provides HTTP/2 binary gRPC streaming, client-driven pull flow control, and schema caching
options.rationale: Pub/Sub API replaces JSON HTTP/1.1 CometD push overhead with high-performance binary Protobuf serialization, backpressure flow control, and dynamic Apache Avro schema lookup.

options.label: Pub/Sub API bypasses event bus allocation limits by streaming directly from database transaction logs
options.distractorAntipattern: Pub/Sub API still enforces standard event bus publishing allocations and does not read raw database transaction logs directly.
options.rationale: Pub/Sub API operates on the Salesforce event bus and respects standard platform event delivery quotas, rather than tailing physical database logs.

options.label: CometD requires synchronous HTTP/1.1 polling intervals that drop events when client queues buffer full
options.distractorAntipattern: CometD uses long polling rather than short polling, but lacks binary compression and fine-grained consumer flow control.
options.rationale: CometD uses HTTP/1.1 Bayeux long polling, which creates heavy JSON serialization overhead and lacks native client backpressure mechanisms.
